solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exacting general acceptance for coinage

parts.note: exacting means hard, demanding
an idea that has currency is generally accepted

explanation.surface: A demanding requirement that everyone accept some new coin or phrase as standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coinage' looks like the minting of a new word, but here it means money itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard currency is stable money, notes and coins trusted internationally, so it is a kind of coinage.

clue.text: Last of those aboard must stop at sea

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so one letter is put within the others

parts.note: must means have to

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The last of the passengers on board must stop while at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave to is the nautical term for bringing a ship to a halt.

clue.text: Touching gift set up musical agent

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, touching on
a present is a gift

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Evita is a Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A moving present arranged for a music agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative acts on behalf of another person, so is an agent.

clue.text: Keen priest cleared out part of church

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief

indicators.note: cleared out means emptied of its inside letters, leaving just the outer ones

explanation.surface: An eager priest cleared out a section of his church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager; it is the verb to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is the underground chamber beneath a church, often used for burials.

clue.text: Carpeting for five authentic houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the other pieces sit within the word for authentic

parts.note: real means authentic
pro means for, in favour of
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Floor covering for five genuine houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' looks like flooring but means a telling-off, as in being carpeted by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carpeted is British slang for being reprimanded, so carpeting is a reproval.

clue.text: Set up monitor primarily to eliminate paper

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the pieces are read backwards
primarily takes only the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: to axe is to cut or eliminate

explanation.surface: A rigged arrangement to get rid of a document, starting with the monitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An examination paper is a test, so an exam is a paper in the school sense.

clue.text: Staff getting to grips with inflections of language

indicators.note: getting to grips with means gripping or holding, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a cane is a walking staff
tones are inflections of the voice

explanation.surface: Staff struggling with the tonal inflections of a foreign language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese is the Chinese language of Guangzhou and Hong Kong, which famously uses tones.

clue.text: Hitch-hiker to board and not alight in border region

indicators.note: to board means to get on, so one piece is put within the others

parts.note: nor means and not
to land is to alight, as a bird does
a hitch-hiker thumbs a lift, so is a thumber

explanation.surface: A hitch-hiker climbs aboard and stays put rather than getting off in the border country.
explanation.walkthrough: NORTHUMBERLAND is the English county bordering Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Northumberland lies on the Anglo-Scottish border, so it is a border region.

clue.text: Tailender from gang entering before old bodyguard leaving

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the letter goes within the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old-fashioned word for before

indicators.note: a tailender comes last, so take the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the SS began as Hitler's bodyguard unit

explanation.surface: A gang's tail-end member slips in before an elderly bodyguard departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' is the noun here, the act of going out.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out or the act of going out, so a leaving.

clue.text: Airline's mechanics initially work well

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Praise for an airline's engineering crew, whose work goes smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Amply means abundantly or fully, an everyday synonym of well as in well provided for.

clue.text: Centuries-old notes regarding golf on steppes

indicators.note: in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y, so the golf-and-regarding pieces follow the steppes

parts.note: steppes are vast grassy plains
on means about or regarding, as in a talk on art
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Ancient music, or a round of golf played out on the Russian steppes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is medieval unaccompanied church chant, music sung for many centuries.

clue.text: Dismissal notice put off, keeping yours truly in Paris

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other
put off suggests disturbed or disordered, so the letters of notice are rearranged

parts.note: yours truly means me, the speaker; in French, as spoken in Paris, I is je

explanation.surface: A notice of dismissal is postponed while the speaker stays in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' looks like postponed but signals the anagram, giving ECTION; 'keeping' places the French pronoun after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejection is a throwing out, so it is a dismissal from a place or post.

clue.text: Item stored in cellar, dry inside trunk

indicators.note: inside places the word for dry within the word for trunk

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, i.e. dry

explanation.surface: Something kept in a dry cellar, or tucked away inside a travelling trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine cellars hold bottles, so a bottle is a typical item stored in one.

clue.text: We're told what manager does in other countries

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than read, a homophone

parts.note: a manager oversees, or supervises, the staff

explanation.surface: A puzzled report on what managers actually do when posted to foreign countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas means abroad, across the sea, so in other countries.

clue.text: Lots of easy work in cracking locks

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so one word is put within the other

parts.note: to secure a door is to lock it, so secures means locks

explanation.surface: A burglar boasts that breaking locks is easy work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post needing little effort, so sinecures are easy jobs.

clue.text: Primates object when pound's replaced old pennies and shillings

indicators.note: replaced says one letter takes the place of another in the word for object

parts.note: to demur is to object
D (denarius) was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money
L (libra) is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
S was the abbreviation for shillings in old British money

explanation.surface: Someone objects to decimal currency replacing old pounds, shillings and pence.
explanation.walkthrough: Pre-1971 British money was pounds, shillings and pence, abbreviated L, S and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are tree-dwelling animals of Madagascar belonging to the primate order.

clue.text: Works out what next in line does

definitions.meaning: a plan that ... works out well
the next in line ..., or follows, the holder of a title

explanation.surface: A plan works out just as the heir takes over.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed means both to turn out well and to follow someone in a role.

clue.text: Series of comments about keeping a number of commandments?

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the word for about wraps the rest

parts.note: CA, circa, means about
there are ten commandments in the Bible

explanation.surface: Remarks made on the Ten Commandments, as if by a biblical commentator.
explanation.definitionFit: A catena is a chain of linked passages, especially a series of commentaries by Church Fathers.

clue.text: Grasp brush, perhaps, scrubbing a pair of taps

indicators.note: scrubbing means wiping out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: brushing is one way to clean, as with teeth
C and H mark the cold and hot taps

explanation.surface: Seize a scrubbing brush to clean a pair of taps.
explanation.definitionFit: To clench something is to grip it tightly, so to grasp it.

clue.text: High copper tap that practitioner struggles to remove?

parts.note: a super, short for superintendent, is a senior police officer, a copper
to bug a phone is to tap it

explanation.surface: A senior police officer taps a phone line, which some practitioner struggles to remove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal, but it is a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A superbug is a drug-resistant bacterium that doctors find very hard to eliminate.

clue.text: Particularly nondescript bears at large

indicators.note: bears means carries, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: grey means dull, nondescript
L is the abbreviation for large in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Especially dull-looking bears roaming free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals, but it is the verb meaning carries.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatly and particularly are both intensifiers meaning especially or to a high degree.

clue.text: England's opening pair caught during match, producing draw

indicators.note: opening pair takes the first two letters of the word it follows
during places one piece within the time, and so the letters, of another

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen are caught out during a cricket match that ends in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' is a cricket result in the surface but means to lure. In cricket the opening pair are the first two batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone in is to attract or lure them, which is to entice.

clue.text: Secret of criminal avoiding punishment

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal's secret is how they escape punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is to escape without any penalty or harm.

clue.text: Roughly beneath tip of elephant's trunk

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath puts the following piece below the earlier one
a tip is an end, so take the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: or so means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: Something lies roughly under the tip of an elephant's trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' looks like the elephant's nose but means the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the human body without head and limbs, also called the trunk.

clue.text: Fuel sanction got round by church

indicators.note: got round by means surrounded by, so the word for church encloses the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to OK something is to sanction it

explanation.surface: A ban on fuel is evaded by the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is the solid residue of coal used as a smokeless fuel.

clue.text: Confirmation of insurance number in private code at last

indicators.note: in places the word for number within the word for private

parts.note: covert means secret or private

indicators.note: at last takes only the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A number in a private code finally confirms an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover note is a temporary document confirming insurance until the policy is issued.

clue.text: Play one's part again to produce a response

definitions.meaning: to ..., with a hyphen, is to act a part once more

explanation.surface: An actor repeats a role in order to get a reaction from the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something, while re-act is to perform a role again.

clue.text: Feast on candies, say, becoming queasy

indicators.note: becoming queasy suggests stomach churning, so the letters are churned up

explanation.surface: Feasting on sweets and feeling sick as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feast' looks like a verb about eating, but it is a church festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascension Day is a Christian festival forty days after Easter, a church feast day.
